packageRules.description: My own packages (hugoh/hk-config, hugoh/gh-workflows, ...) don't need the 7-day soak meant for third-party supply-chain risk: 1 day is enough to catch a bad release. Mirrors renovate-config's default.json, which this config does not extend.

ci.yml's hugoh/go-tools reusable-workflow pins are Copier-owned (regenerated with a version comment on every `copier update`), so keep Renovate's github-actions manager off them to avoid the two racing. Scoped to this file only: a hand-maintained workflow that calls a go-tools reusable workflow (e.g. a repo-specific compat matrix) still gets managed normally.
semantic-pr.yml's hugoh/gh-workflows pin is likewise Copier-owned: it is bumped in go-tools' template and reaches consumers via `copier update`, so Renovate must not also bump it in place.

A go-tools release only reaches a consumer via this Copier-update PR. It lands as the default `chore`: the template changes are dev/CI tooling (mise tool pins, pinned actions) that don't alter the consumer's shipped binary, so they shouldn't cut a consumer release (Go toolchain bumps are handled separately via conf.d/go.toml). First-party, so it takes the 1-day soak: go-tools releases several times a day, and the 7-day third-party soak kept restarting, so the copier PR never matured. The copier datasource is a bare git repo with no release timestamps, so timestamp-optional is required or every release stays pending forever.
mise.ci.toml is NOT Copier-managed (only repos that commit it directly, e.g. for CI-only tools like jj) — let Renovate bump it normally.
